source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Durham's two facilities publish 40 MW of IT capacity, the largest disclosed in North Carolina and 80 percent of the state's disclosed total, but most of the state's data center inventory has no published capacity.

The campus combines DUR1 and DUR2 with 420,000 square feet of technical space. At a nominal 100 kW per rack, that implies roughly 400 racks, or about 1,280 accelerators at 40 kW per GPU and eight GPUs per rack. The operator publishes no breakdown by workload or tenant class, so these are capacity ceilings, not evidence of AI training deployment.

The specifications omit the power infrastructure, PUE, grid operator, and any power purchase agreements. That absence matters for AI because 40 MW of published IT capacity says nothing about how much of it can run continuously or what utilization the local grid permits. North Carolina has 19 mapped facilities, but 14 publish no capacity figures, so Durham's 80 percent share of disclosed capacity may overstate its share of the state's actual compute.
